attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own newsletter post, stated as his own observation.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense statement about Bing's state at publication, framed against Microsoft's claimed fixes. The normalisation is faithful and is correctly classed as an observation.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'easily' and 'egregious misinformation' is ordinary and fair. Reading 'still' as applying at publication fits the present tense. The result turns on that reading, because the one located demonstration was blocked on March 28.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure of the February 17 chat caps. It sets out the background fixes but says nothing about later jailbreaks.

PopSci's independent tests show simple role-play prompts got Bing to produce Sandy Hook conspiracy content in March. Its update says this route was blocked by March 28. That cuts both ways, and under the contract one blocked prompt is not enough to contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: PopSci shows an easy misinformation jailbreak worked in March, but the update says that route was closed before April 2, so the support condition fails. Nothing shows broad testing that every easy bypass was closed, so the contradiction condition also fails. The packet does not settle whether such a jailbreak still worked at publication.
